title: WatchHog
subtitle: Open-source resource monitoring TUI
problem: An 8GB EC2 instance kept locking up on random memory spikes. CloudWatch and Prometheus showed that memory was climbing, never which process caused the crash. We were hard-restarting boxes and losing test data.
solution: A crude polling script emailed the team the top consumers when a threshold was crossed. WatchHog is the compiled Go TUI of that script.
impact: Names the leaking process instead of a 3am mystery restart.
A lightweight open-source TUI so other teams can watch health without a bloated stack.

title: AI-assisted workflows
subtitle: Android and web
problem: The client was locked to an agency for Android and web work. Small UI tweaks took weeks and arrived with a large invoice. Handing the codebase to an AI would have been faster, and reckless with secrets.
solution: I built an internal agent workflow with our codebase, strict commands, and modular skills. Guardrails strip passwords, API keys, and PII before anything reaches the model. An automated test loop has the agent call our backend endpoints and check its own UI and logic before the change is submitted.
impact: Broke the vendor lock-in and cut external development cost.
Week-long agency waits became same-day internal deploys.
No secrets exposed to external LLM providers.

title: Enterprise data lake
subtitle: Automated report infrastructure
problem: Data lived in legacy databases, marketing tools, and spreadsheets. A simple leadership question meant days of CSV exports and Excel. There was no single source of truth.
solution: I designed a data lake as the shared store for the business, with ETL pipelines that collect, clean, and map those sources into one schema. On top of that, a reporting layer lets people generate automated reports or query the data directly.
impact: Fragmented sources became one queryable warehouse.
Three days of manual ops work became instant reports.
Leadership can decide from current numbers.

title: Analytics dashboard
subtitle: High-performance backend
problem: Off-the-shelf analytics were heavy, invasive, and stale. They could not tell us how much traffic came from LLM referrals, or which queries people typed on the page.
solution: I built a small Go backend for concurrent metric tracking with no extra load on the landing page. It records classic SEO signals next to AI-interaction metrics and feeds a custom dashboard.
impact: Fast tracking with no front-end bloat.
Visible insight into how AI search engines reach the site.

title: Otterspace
subtitle: AI-integrated workspace
problem: Project tools are either rigid like Jira or loose like Notion. Most products then drop a generic chatbot into the UI, which gets in the way of engineering work.
solution: Otterspace is an open-source, developer-focused workspace with team assignments and a Notion-like editor. AI shows up only where it helps, for example turning a long feature thread into a structured technical scope.
impact: Building the backend for permissions and rich-text storage.
A quieter, UX-first way to put AI in a product.
